title: Common space of two types recorded by one medium

key_results.statement: The families $(K'^A_h,K'^B_k)$ of self-adjoint operators on $\mathcal H_c$ that give the same $C$ are exactly $K'^A_h=K^A_h+Z$ and $K'^B_k=K^B_k-Z$, with $Z=Z^\dagger$ an arbitrary self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H_c$ (exact).

Under the split, $u^A_h\mapsto u^A_h+z$ and $u^B_k\mapsto u^B_k-z$ with $\lvert z\rangle=(Z-\langle Z\rangle)\lvert\chi\rangle$; the possible shifts $z$ are exactly the vectors of $\mathcal N=\{v\in\mathcal H_c:\langle\chi\vert v\rangle=0\}$.

A function $F$ of the record vectors is well defined (M6) if and only if it is a function of the family $\{w_{hk}\}=\{u^A_h+u^B_k\}$ that is invariant under the common phase $w_{hk}\mapsto e^{i\varphi}w_{hk}$; for example $\lVert\Delta^A_{hh'}\rVert$, $\lVert\Delta^B_{kk'}\rVert$, $g(\Delta^A_{hh'},\Delta^B_{kk'})$ and $\lVert w_{hk}-w_{h'k'}\rVert$ are well defined.
For $\dim\mathcal H_c\ge2$ the set of values of $\lVert u'^A_h-u'^B_k\rVert$ over all splits is $[0,\infty)$, so $\lVert u^A_h-u^B_k\rVert$ is not well defined.

The leading-order distances of the views of $\{a\}$ and $\{b\}$ are $d_0^a(h,h')=\lVert u^A_h-u^A_{h'}\rVert$ and $d_0^b(k,k')=\lVert u^B_k-u^B_{k'}\rVert$ (the setting of package 11 applies to all three cuts); $d_0^a$ depends neither on the $K^B_k$ nor on $\vartheta$.

The leading-order distance of the view of $\{a,b\}$ is $d_0^{ab}((h,k),(h',k'))=\lVert w_{hk}-w_{h'k'}\rVert=\lVert\Delta^A_{hh'}+\Delta^B_{kk'}\rVert$ with $w_{hk}=u^A_h+u^B_k$; its points are $X_{ab}\cong U_A+U_B$ (Minkowski sum), which contains isometric copies of $X_A$ and of $X_B$.

$d_0^{ab}((h,k),(h',k'))^2=d_0^a(h,h')^2+d_0^b(k,k')^2+2g(\Delta^A_{hh'},\Delta^B_{kk'})$, so at leading order the view of $\{a,b\}$ fixes $d_0^a$, $d_0^b$ and the mixed products $g(\Delta^A_{hh'},\Delta^B_{kk'})$, and nothing else; in particular it does not fix any distance between a point of $A$ and a point of $B$.

Let $\pi:D_A\to D_B$ be a bijection between subsets $D_A\subseteq X_A$, $D_B\subseteq X_B$ with $\lvert D_A\rvert\ge2$. Then $\pi$ is a correspondence if and only if $u^A_x-u^A_{x'}=u^B_{\pi(x)}-u^B_{\pi(x')}$ for all $x,x'\in D_A$, i.e. if and only if $u^B_{\pi(x)}=u^A_x+t_\pi$ for all $x\in D_A$ with one vector $t_\pi\in\mathcal N$; equivalently, in some split matched points carry equal record vectors.
Every correspondence is an isometry from $(D_A,d_0)$ onto $(D_B,d_0)$: $d_0^b(\pi(x),\pi(x'))=\lVert u^A_x-u^A_{x'}\rVert=d_0^a(x,x')$; the converse fails (both examples show it).

A correspondence with $D_A=X_A$ and $D_B=X_B$ exists if and only if $\lvert X_A\rvert\ge2$ and $U_B=U_A+t$ for some $t\in\mathcal N$, equivalently $\lvert X_A\rvert=\lvert X_B\rvert\ge2$ and the centred sets agree, $U_A-\bar u^A=U_B-\bar u^B$; it is then unique.

Example (a), $K^A_{h_i}=iX$ and $K^B_{k_j}=jX+Y$ with $\sigma_X>0$: $d_0^a(h_i,h_{i'})=\lvert i-i'\rvert\sigma_X$, $d_0^b(k_j,k_{j'})=\lvert j-j'\rvert\sigma_X$, $d_0^{ab}=\lvert i+j-i'-j'\rvert\sigma_X$ and $g(\Delta^A_{h_ih_{i'}},\Delta^B_{k_jk_{j'}})=(i-i')(j-j')\sigma_X^2$; $X_A$ and $X_B$ are $n$ equally spaced points on a line, $X_{ab}$ is $2n-1$ equally spaced points, and $Y$ drops out of every view.

Example (a) ($K^A_{h_i}=iX$, $K^B_{k_j}=jX+Y$, $\sigma_X>0$): with $\xi=(X-\langle X\rangle)\lvert\chi\rangle$ and $\eta=(Y-\langle Y\rangle)\lvert\chi\rangle$, the correspondences are exactly $\pi_{s,D}:h_i\mapsto k_{i+s}$ on $D$, with $s\in\mathbb Z$, $\lvert s\rvert\le n-2$, $D\subseteq\{h_i:\max(1,1-s)\le i\le\min(n,n-s)\}$, $\lvert D\rvert\ge2$ and $t_\pi=s\xi+\eta$; the unique full correspondence is $h_i\mapsto k_i$ ($s=0$), and the reversal $h_i\mapsto k_{n+1-i}$ is an isometry but not a correspondence.

Example (b), $\mathcal H_c=\mathbb C^2$, $\lvert\chi\rangle=\lvert0\rangle$, $K^A_{h_i}=i\sigma_x$ and $K^B_{k_j}=j\sigma_y$: $d_0^a=\lvert i-i'\rvert$, $d_0^b=\lvert j-j'\rvert$, $d_0^{ab}=\sqrt{(i-i')^2+(j-j')^2}$ and the mixed products vanish; $X_{ab}$ is the $n\times n$ unit square grid in $\mathbb R^2$, and no correspondence exists.

open_issues: Places at d₀ = 0 may be separated at higher orders; there the B-contract operators, and the commutators of the A- and B-contract operators, can enter the view of {a} (out of scope).
Correspondences are defined at leading order only; whether they persist at higher λ, and any rule that selects among the partial correspondences of example (a), are open (out of scope).
d₀ sees only the real Euclidean structure g of the record-vector space; for example, the relative factor i between the two directions of example (b) enters only through orthogonality.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions and rescaling: C, u and d₀ have dimension 1/λ and α ≈ λ d₀ is dimensionless; under C → μC with μ > 0, α(λ; μC) = α(μλ; C), so d₀ → μ d₀, matching u → μ u in (16.8)-(16.10); the correspondence condition (16.11) is homogeneous, so correspondences are unchanged, and Z → μ Z.

k-independent B-contract operators (one operator K for all k): the split with Z = K removes the B-contract, so b decouples, its view stays pure and d₀ of {b} vanishes, as (16.8) gives because all B record vectors are equal; the view of {a,b} is the view of {a} times the pure state of b, so its d₀ equals that of {a}, as (16.9) gives; there is a single point of type B, so no correspondence exists, and the mixed products vanish.

Exchange of the roles of a and b: the split (16.3) maps to itself with Z → -Z, the two formulas of (16.8) are exchanged, (16.9) is symmetric, and the correspondence condition (16.11) becomes the same condition for the inverse map with t → -t, as the symmetric definition requires.
